newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BHP says picked for Angola oil concession.
newsitem.headline: BHP says picked for Angola oil concession.

text.p: Australian-based Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd has been invited by Angola's state oil company Sonangol to be the operator of one of its deepwater oil concessions, an official said on Tuesday.
"We have been invited by Sonangol as operator for Block 21, but it is still early days," the company official, speaking from London, said.
"If everything goes according to plan we will sign the production sharing agreement closer to the end of the year," the official added.
Block 21, just south of the Angolan capital Luanda, was heavily bid by top international companies and is one of the several new deepwater fields off Angola.
Angola is the second largest producer of oil in sub-Saharan Africa with over 700,000 barrels of oil produced per day.
Industry analysts say production levels are expected to rise considerably as deepwater production gets underway.
BHP is one of Australia's biggest companies and has diverse minerals, petroleum and steel interests.
